target_scope: Representative breadth of common single-threaded application code. The user's 80% goal is a practical design aspiration, not a measured population percentage or CPU-sample attribution target.
interpretation: Assess each operation family and composed application separately. Matching performance across these workloads supports confidence for applications with similar operations, input shapes, working sets and lifetimes. Do not infer a percentage of real codebases from case counts or CPU samples, and do not let one library win offset unrelated weaknesses.

limits: bounded integer ranges and exact dyadic floats
repeated warm fixtures
no broader numerical kernels or varied branch histories
small warm working sets
limited record/list shape variety
no large cache-miss-heavy traversal
repetitive text and limited Unicode shapes
no large documents, normalization or regular expressions
compact keys and repeated insertion patterns
no deletion/tombstones or large diverse-key workloads
small scalar records and helpers
no recursion, captured closures, FFI or managed-field record workloads
fixed variant shapes and error mixes
no large recursive variants or complex unwinding
short-allocation work may be optimized away
no long-lived mixed-lifetime heap churn or tail-latency evidence
snapshot costs include native COW versus explicit cloning
specific library APIs and input patterns
Go sort.Slice/sort.SliceStable, not generic slices APIs
limited key distributions
five distinct words in an eight-token pattern
no high-cardinality corpus or streaming

csv_aggregate.represents: quote-aware text parsing, numeric validation and grouped aggregation
limits: declared CSV subset and repeated row shapes
no embedded newlines or large varied documents

json_transform.represents: native JSON parse, filter/rebuild and serialization
limits: one schema and native library differences
no deep nesting, varied schemas or streaming

packet_decode.represents: byte decoding, validation and success/error handling
limits: fixed ten-byte format and validity mix
no networking or general protocol-throughput claim

lox_eval.represents: tagged values, operand stack, variables, control flow and function calls
limits: execution-only fixed bytecode subset
no complete frontend, classes, closures or dynamic name lookup

confidence_gaps: large working sets and cache-miss-heavy access
map deletion, high-cardinality and varied-length keys
varied text, numeric and structured-data shapes
concurrency, synchronization, asynchronous scheduling and I/O
